answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring every identity to continuously operate a private compute harbor whose output is attested from a shared validation terrace. Each new inlet of traffic must carry a fresh, non-reusable proof of unique resource consumption that cannot be cloned without duplicating the hardware and energy cost. An attacker wanting N identities must fund N separate harbors and keep them online; the terrace rejects any inlet whose proof collides or arrives late, so mass duplication collapses under linear real-world expense.
